explanation: An empty Optional holds no Tracked. emplace constructs one in place; emplacing again destroys the old value first. value_or copies the value, or builds the fallback from the int only when empty. value() on an empty Optional throws std::bad_optional_access (-4).
Copy assignment: both engaged -> copy-assign the value; only the source engaged -> copy-construct; only the target engaged -> destroy its value; both empty -> nothing.
Moving from an engaged Optional moves its value and leaves the source engaged, holding a moved-from value (-1), as std::optional does.
An empty Optional never constructs, assigns or destroys a value, whatever is done to it.
Optional(const T&) copy-constructs once, Optional(T&&) move-constructs once.
The destructor destroys an engaged value exactly once and an empty Optional destroys nothing.
reset destroys the value once; resetting an empty Optional does nothing.
emplace on an engaged Optional destroys the old value and constructs the new one in place from the forwarded arguments: no copy, no move, no assignment.
If T's constructor throws in emplace, the exception propagates, the old value has already been destroyed and the Optional is empty.
value(), operator* and operator-> all reach the same object, stored inside the Optional.
value_or copies the value if engaged (a moved-from value is still a value: -1); otherwise it constructs T from the fallback, once.
Copy construction copy-constructs the value (if any) into the new Optional's own storage.
Both engaged: assign the value (T's copy assignment), do not destroy and reconstruct.
Only the source engaged: construct the value (the target's storage holds no object to assign to).
Only the target engaged: destroy its value; the target becomes empty.
Move assignment follows the same four cases with move-assign / move-construct; a moved-from source stays engaged.
A moved-from Optional is not reset: it still holds a (moved-from) value that its destructor destroys.
o = o and o = std::move(o) leave o as it was.
emplace perfectly forwards its arguments (an rvalue stays an rvalue).
